reviewContext.userProblem: flying-mail (Cloudflare Worker mailcal-api with D1 mailcal-db) has an unauthenticated first-caller-wins bootstrapAdmin, an optional open self-signup mode, no bot protection on the passwordless login-link request, no per-IP rate limiting of the unauthenticated auth mutations, and is reachable on workers.dev where zone-level DDoS/WAF protections do not apply.
requiredOutcomes: bootstrapAdmin requires the one-time token from Worker secret FLYING_MAIL_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN (hash plus constant-time compare), is disabled with SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE when the secret is unset, works only on an empty instance, cannot succeed again; mise task bootstrap-admin and CLI admin bootstrap exist and are documented.

FLYING_MAIL_SIGNUP and SignupMode are removed; createUser (admin only) sends an invitation email with a single-use sign-in link (default TTL 7 days, FLYING_MAIL_INVITE_TTL_SECONDS bounded 86400-2592000); resendInvitation is admin-only and throttled; Settings > Users shows Invite user, invitation status and resend.

requestEmailAuth requires a Turnstile token when FLYING_MAIL_TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY is set, verified server-side via siteverify with remoteip from CF-Connecting-IP, hostname and action 'login' checks; publicConfig { turnstileSiteKey } is public; the login page renders the widget explicitly and resets after each attempt; CSP adds only https://challenges.cloudflare.com to script-src and frame-src.

requestEmailAuth, verifyEmailAuthToken and bootstrapAdmin are rate limited per IP and operation through a RateLimiter port (Workers binding, in-memory and fake adapters); exceeding returns GraphQL error RATE_LIMITED at HTTP 200 without user enumeration; the per-email LOGIN throttle is kept.

nonGoals: No deploy, no remote wrangler, no Turnstile widget, DNS, custom domain or secret creation (orchestrator owns all live Cloudflare operations).
No git commit, push, stash, reset or checkout by workers.
No Turnstile on verifyEmailAuthToken, bootstrapAdmin, the /auth/verify page or authenticated operations.
No revocation of earlier invitation links on resend.
No single D1 batch for bootstrap user, key and scope writes.
No HTTP 429 path; no WAF or zone rules.
No passwords; no new heavy dependencies; no Turnstile wrapper package.
constraints: AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md: English only, no emojis, maximum TypeScript strictness, Biome clean, ts-coding-standards, no touched file at 1000+ lines.
Never edit or squash migrations 0001-0014; only apps/api/migrations/0015_auth_hardening.sql is added and must apply on top of the existing history.
Never commit secret values; secrets via kinko exec and wrangler secret put.
Turnstile and rate limiting are null (disabled) at the port level when unconfigured so local Bun development and tests run without Cloudflare; the Worker config enables both.
Uniform responses: checks before user lookup (rate limit, Turnstile, configuration) never depend on the email.
Invitation and login emails contain a plain extractable https sign-in URL alone on its own line in the text part and as an href in the HTML part.

Workers edit only their plan writePaths and their own plan Progress Log; impl-plans/PROGRESS.json and impl-plans/README.md are edited only by auth-hardening-09; no worker edits this dispatch manifest.
Record sha256 before and after each edit; on drift re-read and reapply only the plan's intent; never revert others' edits; no repository-wide formatters.
Evidence for each plan and attempt goes under tmp/auth-hardening-s305/<planId>/<attempt>/ (gitignored); plan 09 gate logs go to /tmp/flying-mail-auth-hardening/.
designDecisionsAndRationale: Bootstrap token is a GraphQL mutation argument passed as a variable (schema-validated, no auth-middleware change); compare constantTimeEqual(hash(token), hash(secret)) before createFirstUser so a tokenless caller cannot learn whether the instance is bootstrapped (design 3.2-3.3).

One-time guarantee rests on the atomic insert-if-empty createFirstUser and the users-never-deleted invariant; no separate consumed marker because a D1 wipe is the intended re-provisioning path (design 3.4).

Invitations reuse email-auth challenges with a required purpose column (LOGIN | INVITATION) so the LOGIN 3-per-15-minutes throttle and TTL stay intact; users gain invitation_accepted_at (migration 0015, design 4.2).
Single-use links use an atomic conditional consume UPDATE instead of find-then-save (design 4.5).
RATE_LIMITED is a GraphQL error at HTTP 200 because all /graphql failures route on extensions.code and a multi-field document has no single status (design 2.2).
Client IP: Worker trusts only CF-Connecting-IP; Bun/Node server uses only the socket peer address; null maps to the key segment 'unknown' (design 2.1).
One AUTH_RATE_LIMITER binding, simple = { limit = 10, period = 60 }, key auth:<operation>:<ip>; Workers adapter fails open, siteverify adapter fails closed (design 6.1-6.2, 5.2).

Fail-fast config: secret without site key, secret without public origin, or a bootstrap token under 32 characters throws during composition; a site key without secret is silently disabled (design 3.1, 5.1).
workers_dev = false plus preview_urls = false and a custom domain route so zone protections cannot be bypassed via workers.dev (design 7.1).

Plan DAG: wave 1 (01, 02, 03, 04) -> wave 2 (05, 06) -> wave 3 (07) -> wave 4 (08) -> wave 5 (09 serial reconciliation); 07 depends on 02 for the _headers CSP equality test; 08 depends on 07 for the end-to-end CF-Connecting-IP test and on 02 for the dry-run assets.
intentionalTradeoffs: P1 (pending user confirmation, default applied): the bootstrap API key secret is written to .private/bootstrap-admin-api-key (exclusive create, 0600) and only the prefix is printed.
P2 (pending, default applied): half-configured Turnstile or a short bootstrap token fails fast and takes the Worker down with a masked 500 until fixed.
P3 (pending, default applied): Workers rate limiting is per-location, approximate and fails open on binding errors.
Serialising 07 and 08 lengthens the critical path to five waves.
IPR-L1: both test fakes live in packages/application/src/test-support/auth-hardening-fakes.ts (re-exported from fakes.ts) instead of design 5.2's fake-turnstile-verifier.ts name.
Typecheck noise inside waves 1 and 2 is possible (plans 01-06 run scoped typechecks); plan 09's full gate is authoritative.
supportedEdgeCases: Wrong token on a non-empty instance returns FORBIDDEN, not CONFLICT; second bootstrap with the correct token returns CONFLICT.
Rate-limited calls return RATE_LIMITED before the token check, Turnstile verification or any user lookup, identically for known and unknown emails.
Missing or invalid Turnstile token returns FORBIDDEN 'Verification failed. Please retry.' identically for known and unknown emails; with Turnstile disabled the token is ignored.
Concurrent double verification of one token yields exactly one session.
An invitation link after acceptance is invalid; a LOGIN link for a pending user accepts the invitation.
INVITATION challenges do not count toward the LOGIN throttle and vice versa; the 4th invitation within 24 hours is RATE_LIMITED.
Mail unconfigured on createUser returns SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE before any write; a send failure after save leaves the user PENDING and resendable.
Worker ignores X-Forwarded-For; local server ignores CF-Connecting-IP and X-Forwarded-For.
CLI refuses to run without FLYING_MAIL_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN or when the secret file exists, before any network call; the secret never reaches stdout or stderr.
outOfScopeEdgeCases: Partial bootstrap failure leaving an admin without an API key (admin can still sign in by email; residual risk).
Exact global rate-limit quotas across Cloudflare locations.
Future user deletion features (must add a persisted bootstrap marker in the same change).
namespace_id collisions on the Cloudflare account (orchestrator adjusts at deploy time).
residualRisks: Typecheck noise in waves 1 and 2; plan 09 gate authoritative.
User confirmations P1-P4 pending with defaults implemented.
